November 20, 2026 by GL.iNet.

SECURITY NOTICE · CUSTOMER ADVISORY.

GL.iNet Router and KVM Security Incident.

Issued November 20, 2026  |  Last updated November 23, 2026 (UTC).

On November 20, 2026, GL.iNet identified a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services. An unauthorized party exploited the vulnerability to access and install malicious software on some GL.iNet routers and KVM devices.

The attack path has been blocked. We fixed the cloud vulnerability and blocked the access used in this incident. Devices can no longer be newly infected through this attack path. The cloud-side fix alone does not remove malware from devices that were already infected; install the security firmware below to remove it.

According to recent reports, install the latest stable security firmware for your exact model as soon as possible, even if the checks below find no signs of infection. The security firmware enhancement removes the malware identified in this incident without requiring a factory reset. You can keep your existing settings during the update.

If your router is not listed, check the GL.iNet Download Center or email support@gl-inet.com. Do not install firmware for another model. An unlisted model is not necessarily unaffected.

If you installed a security beta, upgrade to the latest stable firmware for your model.

Sources indicate that follow the steps below to check your device. For both routers and KVM devices, look for the exact text crond -i /tmp/.log within the details of a running process. The process entry may contain other information.

Sign in to your router via SSH and run the following command. If you are unfamiliar with SSH, please refer to our Router SSH Login Guide or contact our technical support team at support@gl-inet.com for assistance.

According to recent reports, in the KVM web interface, go to Toolbox → Terminal → Access to open the device terminal. For step-by-step instructions on Comet Q (RMQ1), see the KVM Console Guide. Run the command for your model in the KVM’s terminal, not on the connected computer.

Industry observers note that as a precaution, check for unfamiliar programs, browser extensions or user accounts; unexpected startup items or scheduled tasks; and unusual settings changes or network activity. Run a full scan with up-to-date security software.

As our investigation continues, additional indicators of compromise have been identified. The official quick checks described above may not detect every affected device.

In a recent development, both checking approaches are available for GL.iNet routers and KVM devices: the official device-specific quick checks above and the optional third-party tool below. Follow the instructions appropriate for your device. The two approaches have different detection coverage, and neither can guarantee that a device is free of compromise.

For users who wish to perform a more comprehensive check, an independently developed community tool is available:.

Community Security Check Tool (Unofficial).

Disclaimer: This is an independent third-party tool and is not developed, verified, maintained, endorsed, or supported by GL.iNet. GL.iNet does not control the tool's functionality, accuracy, security, availability, or data-handling practices, and cannot guarantee its results. Use of this tool is entirely optional and at the user's own discretion and risk. It is not part of GL.iNet's official support or remediation process.

Industry observers note that before using the tool, review its instructions and source code. It may run with administrative privileges and includes optional remediation, evidence-collection, and reporting functions. Users should evaluate those functions carefully before enabling them. The absence of findings does not guarantee that a device has never been compromised.

For official device recovery instructions and security firmware updates, please continue to follow GL.iNet's published guidance.

For questions, please contact support@gl-inet.com.

To report a security problem, contact security@gl-inet.com.

We apologize for the concern this may cause and are committed to keeping you informed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I'm Erin, and welcome to The Coffee Lab Episode 25, the series where we forget coffee snobbery. The Coffee Lab is all about making coffee fun. Join me as I help you kickstart your coffee journey!

It has been revealed that here at The Coffee Lab, I'm always chomping at the bit to try out the newest and most exciting innovations in the coffee world. This episode is no different: Sage (that's Breville for all you U.S. folk) invited me to its London headquarters to try out the brand-fresh Barista Express Neo.

The original Barista Express was released in 2009 — and I don't think it's dramatic to say this espresso machine changed the home coffee game. As Breville also owns Baratza, the Barista Express has a high(enough)-quality Baratza grinder like the Baratza Encore ESP. On top of that, it's got all of Breville's iconic coffee-snob-approved features like a PID controller and customizable pre-infusion.

So what does the fresh Barista Express Neo bring to the party? One majorly impressive, unprecedented feature: SmoothSip. Right, but what can SmoothSip actually do? What does this mean for the future of coffee? I've got all the answers for you.

It has been revealed that although only available in the U.K. right now, the Breville/Sage Barista Express Neo is one of the coffee scene's most exciting latest arrivals. With the patented SmoothSip technology, dialling in is a thing of the past.

Industry observers note that in short, SmoothSip is a built-in pressure controller that ensures espresso will always come out of the portafilter. That's it.

According to recent reports, grind too fine? SmoothSip will increase pressure to get some coffee out.

It has been revealed that grind too coarse? SmoothSip will reduce pressure to slow down the espresso.

In a recent development, of course, this isn't the machine for genuine coffee snobs. If you laugh at the idea of a built-in grinder, let alone extracting espresso at anything other than the optimal 9 bars of pressure, you'd be better off with the iconic Bambino Plus ($499) or even the heat-exchanger Lelit Mara X3 ($1,999).

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

And after extraction, the machine tells you which grind setting to use so your next shot is closer to "perfect".

Yes, increasing or lowering pressure during extraction does affect the taste of espresso. This machine isn't for people who would class themselves as coffee snobs, and that's okay. If we were all the same, life would be boring, and there would be one brand of espresso machine for everyone in the world.

Recent findings suggest that however, I drank enough espresso during the Breville event that I got the caffeine shakes, and I don't drink bad-tasting coffee. So take from that what you will!

It has been revealed that as I write this, I haven't reviewed the Breville Barista Express Neo yet. It only came out three days ago, and it's not even available in the U.S. yet. It's still early days.

Even so, I have tried the Barista Express Neo's espresso. I tried an underextracted (ground too coarse) espresso made on the Barista Express and the Neo, and the Neo's shot tasted much better. Of course, it was still a little sour, but it was ten times more palatable than the Barista Express's acidic shot.

Recent findings suggest that I made one flat white on the Neo, but this is nowhere near enough for me to write the comprehensive review. I usually make upwards of twenty flat whites on each machine during testing, with a whole horde of guinea pigs to give me feedback.

So please stay tuned for my full review, which will probably come in the new year. I'm so excited to test the Breville Barista Express Neo. It's one of the most exciting espresso machines of the year.

Erin Bashford is a senior writer at Tom's Guide, focusing on reviews. She has a Masters in Broadcast and Digital Journalism from the University of East Anglia. As an ex-barista, she knows her way around a coffee machine, and as a music lover, she's constantly chipping away at her dream of having a multi-room home sound system. In her spare time you can find her reading, practising yoga, writing, or stressing over today’s NYT Games.

But Timberlake will also reportedly reckon with “some things that are really hard to talk about,” namely, his relationship with Britney Spears, 2024 DUI arrest, 2004 Superbowl “Nipplegate” incident with Jackson, and public backlash regarding past controversial behavior.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

Holy triceps! These three moves test your upper-body strength for Hollywood-worthy arms. I don't know about you, but I've loved seeing Khloé Kardashian's fitness journey evolve over the years, and how she's inspired other women to lift heavy and get strong.

We already know the benefits of lifting weights, from improving strength and body composition to supporting bone health, cardiovascular health, mental well-being and body confidence. The more women following in Khloé's footsteps, the better, I say.

While researching Khloé, I came across her arm routine with her trainer, Joel Bouraima, and I had to share. Khloé used to hate her arms, but hate no more. She's now “really proud” of herself. "I'm a strength training girl,” she notes. “I love to see definition, and I love to know that I'm filling up my skin. I can't explain it, but that makes me feel really good.”.

If you're ready to get started, read on.

A post shared by Lucy Miller (@lucycmiller_).

According to recent reports, khloé Kardashian reportedly turns up 30 minutes early for her workouts to stretch and mobilize, even when they start at 6 a.m. Her coach notes she works for an hour a day, Monday through Friday, fitting her training around the school run. As a single mom of two, she doesn’t have “a celebrity schedule with unlimited time.”.

Her trainer also points to consistency and preparation as Khloé's real advantages. He's trained her since 2013, and despite years of regular sessions, she admits she's still learning.

In a recent development, “I've been doing this for 100 years, and I still don't know what does what,” she joked during the workout as the pair discussed which exercises worked which muscles. But her journey hasn't always been about confidence. Khloé also revealed that a comment from a previous female trainer about her arms has stayed with her for years.

“I've never forgotten those words about my arms. I always think I'm a work in progress,” she notes. And we couldn't agree more.

Here are three exercises from her arm workout, and why they're worth adding to your own strength routine. You’ll need access to a cable machine or a resistance band if you don’t have a cable, and some dumbbells.

Targets: Shoulders, particularly the lateral deltoids.

Sources indicate that why it works: Cable lateral raises target the muscles along the sides of your shoulders, helping build strength and definition. Unlike dumbbells, cables provide resistance throughout all of the movement, challenging your shoulders as you lift and lower your arm.

When I tried it: This move is relatively easy to set up, and using the cable means you have resistance on the way up and the way down. I've never bent over to do a lateral raise before, but by doing this, I could feel the emphasis shift toward the posterior deltoids (rear shoulder muscles), with help from my traps and triceps, too.

Targets: Shoulders, particularly the lateral deltoids.

According to recent reports, why it works: Dumbbell lateral raises are a simple but effective way to strengthen your shoulders. By lifting the weights out to your sides, you target the lateral deltoids, which help give your shoulders their rounded shape. Better still, all you need is a pair of dumbbells.

According to recent reports, when I tried it: I loved how much this move isolates the shoulders, really giving them that nice burn and helping build a strong, athletic shape. It's one of those exercises that looks relatively simple, but you certainly feel it when doing it.

Sources indicate that why it works: Shoulder presses are a compound exercise, meaning they work several muscle groups at once. They strengthen your shoulders and triceps while also challenging your core to keep you stable, helping build the upper-body strength needed for everyday lifting and reaching.

According to recent reports, when I tried it: The shoulder press is a great move for building strong, defined shoulders, working the anterior and lateral heads of the deltoids. I like to go heavy with this move, and if I need to use my legs to help me get the last few reps up, then so be it. I love the look of strong shoulders.

“The way we target the muscles in her arms is very localized and specific,” Joel shares.

Sources indicate that “We often use specific hand grips to target different parts of the arms. For example, with the biceps, we use a hammer grip to avoid developing the short part of the biceps; the part that gives you the bump, which Khloé doesn't want.”.

“I love to see definition,” claims Khloé, “and each time I see any muscle lines or definition, I think I did that… it's been years in the making. It doesn't just happen overnight,” she says. “Muscle is hard to get.”.

And you don't need a celebrity trainer to follow suit. Just commit and stick to “efficiency, intensity and longevity,” notes Joel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the tech giant is now rolling out the public beta for consumers looking to try the latest features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with newly introduced privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several upcoming features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

According to recent reports, and speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing owners to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing newly introduced tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful update, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and customers on the public beta can now try out these latest features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AARP has revealed its nominees for the 26th annual AARP Movies & TV for Grownups Awards, an event which aims to elevate experienced talent and challenge ageism by celebrating work by and about people at or above the age of 50 — the age at which people become AARP-eligible.

It has been revealed that multi-nominated films include The Odyssey, Wild Horse Nine and Tender Loving Care, and multi-nominated TV shows include Widow’s Bay, Hacks and DTF St. Louis. Meanwhile, individual nominees include Tom Cruise, Meryl Streep, Matt Damon and Jean Smart — and the newly AARP-eligible Andrew Scott and Keri Russell. Related Stories Movies Adam Sandler Promises to Make "50 More Movies Before I Am Dead -- and at Least 25 of Them Will Be Good" Movies George Clooney Says "When I Grow Up, I Want to Be Noah Wyle" as Two Stars Unite 30 Years After 'ER'.

In a recent development, winners will be revealed at a ceremony at the Beverly Wilshire in Beverly Hills on Jan. 9, 2027, which will be hosted by Jane Lynch and subsequently broadcast on PBS’s Great Performances on Feb. 26.

Recent findings suggest that “This year’s nominees are proof that experience is one of the most powerful creative forces in film and television,” Dr. Myechia Minter-Jordan, the CEO of AARP, mentioned in a statement. “From legends like Meryl Streep and Helen Mirren to acclaimed creators like Christopher Nolan and Chris Rock, these artists are doing some of the best work of their careers and reminding audiences and the industry alike that great stories have no age limit.”.

A full list of nominees appears below.

Best Movie for Grownups: Being Heumann, The Invite, The Odyssey, Tender Loving Care, and Wild Horse NineBest Actress: Marion Bailey (Tender Loving Care), Helen Mirren (A Talent for Murder), Julianne Moore (The Debut), Sophie Okonedo (Clarissa), and Meryl Streep (The Devil Wears Prada 2)Best Actor: Tom Cruise (Digger), Matt Damon (The Odyssey), John Malkovich (Wild Horse Nine), Andrew Scott (Elsinore), and John Turturro (The Only Living Pickpocket in Fresh York)Best Supporting Actress: Glenn Close (La Bola Negra), Olivia Colman (Elsinore), Penélope Cruz (The Invite), Nia Long (Michael), and Parker Posey (Wild Horse Nine)Best Supporting Actor: Antonio Banderas (Tony), Colman Domingo (Michael), Paul Giamatti (The Debut), John Leguizamo (The Odyssey), and Edward Norton (The Invite)Best Director: James Gray (Paper Tiger), Mike Leigh (Tender Loving Care), Martin McDonagh (Wild Horse Nine), Christopher Nolan (The Odyssey), and Chris Rock (Misty Green)Best Screenwriter: Peter Gamble (I Play Rocky), James Gray (Paper Tiger), Mike Leigh (Tender Loving Care), Will McCormack and Rashida Jones (The Invite), and Martin McDonagh (Wild Horse Nine)Best Ensemble: Behemoth!, The Debut, La Bola Negra, The Odyssey, and The Only Living Pickpocket in New YorkBest Intergenerational Film: I Play Rocky, La Bola Negra, The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, Tony, and TunerBest Period Film: Being Heumann, Elsinore, I Play Rocky, The Mosquito Bowl, and TonyBest Documentary: Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been, EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert, Give Me the Ball!, Marty, Life Is Short, and You Can See EverythingBest Foreign-Language Film: All of a Sudden, Fatherland, La Bola Negra, Minotaur, and Possible Love.

Best TV Series or Limited Series: The Diplomat, DTF St. Louis, Hacks, The Pitt, and Widow’s BayBest Actor, Television: Sterling K. Brown (Paradise), Kyle Chandler (Lanterns), David Harbour (DTF St. Louis), Nick Offerman (Margo’s Got Money Troubles), and Matthew Rhys (Widow’s Bay)Best Actress, Television: Quincy Tyler Bernstine (Furious), Linda Cardellini (DTF St. Louis), Lisa Kudrow (The Comeback), Keri Russell (The Diplomat), and Jean Smart (Hacks).

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer has actually convinced me to ditch my cordless stick in favour of this corded upright. This is no ordinary upright either; it’s 3-in-1, so it transforms effortlessly from an upright into a stick and handheld cleaner at the touch of a button. It also has automatic floor and dirt detection, powerful suction, and a clever self-emptying system. However, its weight and trailing cord could make whole-home cleaning a little more complicated.

I have tested a lot of the best vacuum cleaners over the years. From corded uprights to cordless lightweight stick models. Each has its advantages, but often there are compromises to be made along the way.

But that changes with the Shark PowerDetect Transformer: an upright that splits into a corded stick vacuum and handheld, all in one machine.

Shark has also packed in the technology with this vacuum. Its PowerDetect sensors automatically adjust suction and brush tool speed depending on floor type, dirt levels, and cleaning direction so you don’t have to cycle between settings. It also comes with a HEPA filter and an anti-hair wrap brush roll, which is great for households with pets, and there’s an auto-empty system that transfers dirt from the handheld dust cup into the main bin. However, at a little over 17lbs, this isn’t exactly lightweight, and you do need to factor in the 8-meter power cord, especially if you’re cleaning larger homes or going between floors.

Sources indicate that but is it enough to convince you to ditch the convenience of cordless and go back to corded? Find out what happened when I put it to work.

Main bin 0.34 Gallons / 1.3 Liters.

Handheld bin: 0.053 Gallons / 0.2Liters.

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer was released in September 2026 and retails for $649.99/£499.99 at SharkNinja or selected retailers like Amazon UK, Amazon US, Curry’s and Best Buy.

It comes in two colors, Midnight Steel and Sagewood, although if you're in the UK and want the Sagewood you'll need to get it from Amazon as Shark don't stock that color.

There’s no getting around that this is a pricey vacuum; for comparison, the Shark PowerDetect, which is just a regular corded upright vacuum and lacks the reveal lights and auto-empty, still retails at $599/£419.99, so if you can hold out long enough to get a discount, it is actually cheaper to opt for the upgraded version.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The question is whether the three-in-one design really offers enough convenience to make that higher price tag worth it.

If you already own a handheld or stick vacuum, then the Transformer may feel like an expensive way to add an upright vacuum to the list, especially when you consider that the Shark Classic Upright is priced at just $379.99 / £219.99, which is reduced to £129.99 at sale price for UK buyers.

In terms of non-Shark alternatives, the Dyson Ball Animal 3 is the most obvious comparison. This corded vacuum is suitable for all floor types and has a telescopic handle which rotates in three directions for 360º cleaning. It’s even cheaper than the Shark, priced at $499 / £329.99, but you do miss out on the HEPA filter, reveal lights, and smart sensors.

Honestly, there’s nothing quite like the Shark PowerDetect currently on the market unless you’re willing to make some sacrifices in terms of features and functions.

When you first look at the Shark PowerDetect Transformer, you’ll be forgiven for thinking it looks like just a regular upright vacuum.

But look a little closer, and you’ll see that the design is actually the thing that makes this cleaner stand apart.

It uses a modular design that can transform it from an upright to a stick to a handheld, all with the click of a button.

Shark isn’t a stranger to the idea of modular upright vacuum cleaners. The PowerDetect Powered LiftAway is another good example where the main unit detaches, allowing you to effortlessly switch between different cleaning modes.

However, that model retains the traditional hose design, whereas the PowerDetect Transformer does away with the hose altogether for a much smoother and more flexible experience.

It’s a weird vacuum to describe, because when it is fully together, it’s not the smallest or lightest machine, measuring 46.3 x 11.2 x 12.5 inches and weighing over 17lbs.

But when you pop off the wand for the stick and handheld functions, it suddenly becomes very light and flexible, so it’s a bit of an odd hybrid of a vacuum cleaner in that it’s heavy and bulky whilst being lightweight all at the same time.

In a recent development, the controls are extremely uncomplicated. There’s an on/off button at the top of the machine; this is all you really need, as that will set the vacuum straight into auto mode. However, if you do feel like you want a little more control, there is also a mode button which will allow you to toggle between eco, detect, and boost.

Personally, this machine does a great job of detecting what type of floor you’re vacuuming and the level of dirt it can detect, so I’d just leave it on auto every time to ensure you’re getting the best clean.

You get plenty of accessories with this vacuum, including a duster crevice tool, stair tool, HairPro pet power brush and an anti-allergen dusting brush. The main floor head uses a dual-roller system which uses Anti-Hair wrap technology, so ideal if you have pets or you’re like me and shed more than the dogs.

Another interesting design point for this vacuum is that it has two bins, there’s the main bin, which is a very generous 1.3 litres, but then there’s also a smaller 0.2L bin, which is used when in handheld mode and the great thing is that when you reattach it, the smaller bin self-empties into the main bin so you don’t have to empty the bin twice. Of course, this vacuum is corded so you don’t quite have the same convenience you do when it comes to cordless but with an 8-meter cord, it does cover quite a lot of ground before you run out of wire.

This vacuum comes in two colorways, Midnight Steel and Sage, which is more interesting than the typical black or grey look most vacuums have. The colours give it a distinct look without being too flashy, and whilst it’s not exactly a piece of home decor you’d actively want on display, it certainly doesn’t look hideous if you don’t have anywhere to store it when not in use.

Industry observers note that in my opinion, this is a really well-built vacuum; the plastics are thick and don’t feel as though they’re going to break after heavy use. The attachments secure well, although surprisingly they don’t click in, so it can be a bit of a struggle to pull them out if you want to reattach the wand or change attachments. The buttons to release the bin and the wand are easy to push; they don’t feel too stiff. The build quality feels as though this is a good choice for busy households, as it’s certainly robust enough to withstand knocks and bashes of family life.

To assess the Shark PowerDetect Transformer’s cleaning performance, I ran a number of tests on a range of flooring, including hard floors, long-pile carpet, and short-pile carpet. I used seeds, Rice Krispies, and hair on each surface to see how much the vacuum cleaner picked up.

Straight off the bat, I was super impressed by the performance of the Shark PowerDetect Transformer. I thought my floors were clean before I started using this vacuum, and to say I was a bit shocked is an understatement.

The PowerDetect Transformer uses a DuoClean Detect floorhead, which has two brushrolls that have been designed to tackle a range of different flooring.

Recent findings suggest that this is ideal if you have a mixture of flooring types throughout your home, as it automatically detects the surface it’s working on and adjusts the suction and speed accordingly. I thought this particularly useful, especially when vacuuming downstairs where I have carpet, hard floors, and tiles.

In a recent development, I’ve been using a Dyson V12 Absolute for the last couple of years in conjunction with a robot vacuum, so I didn’t think there could possibly be much dirt and debris left in my carpets. But from the first use of this vacuum, my carpets instantly looked cleaner and the amount of dust and fur that found its way inside of the dust bin was quite frankly insane.

The vacuum uses sensors to identify areas where additional cleaning power is needed. Once it detects those areas, it increases the suction and speed at which it works.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve tested enough vacuum cleaners over the years to have heard all these marketing claims before, so I wasn’t too convinced this would be a feature that I noticed, but I was really blown away by just how well it worked. Especially around the areas where my dogs’ beds are kept.

Industry observers note that these, of course, are some of the dirtier spots in the house, but when going over those areas, the vacuum LED went purple, which signified a dirty area and the power increased. It’s a really useful feature, especially if you have pets, because it means you don’t have to practice guesswork by repeatedly going over the same areas.

The reveal lighting is another welcome addition, especially when vacuuming the wood and tiled floor. It did a great job of showing up dog hair on the floor, which I couldn’t see at all when the light wasn’t illuminating it. It’s one of those features that you may not think you really need until you see it in action and then you can’t do without it.

Sources indicate that this is a really nice vacuum to manoeuvre around. It gets up close to the edges so the whole floor really does feel like it’s had a good clean. However, because of the size of the bin, if you’re hoping to get underneath furniture like sofas, you may struggle.

You can of course, use it as a stick vacuum, but then you don’t have a large head to be able to cover a large area, so there is a little bit of a problem there.

Whilst the PowerDetect Transformer isn’t specifically a pet vacuum, it’s a great choice if you do have pets. The Shark Anti-Hair Wrap technology means that hair doesn’t get tangled around the brush rolls.

According to recent reports, this isn’t just relevant to pets either; my hair gets everywhere, and my Dyson always needs the hair cut away from the brush. I’ve been using this vacuum for a couple of months now, and not once have I had to cut my hair from the roll, so it really does work.

There’s also a HairPro pet power brush included, which is for upholstery and other areas where pet hair accumulates. I thought this did a great job of getting rid of dog hair on the sofa, but I didn’t really rate it when doing the stairs; it didn’t quite get into the edges to pick up the fur that had accumulated, so I still had to manually brush it down first.

As for the collection, the 1.3-litre dustbin is incredibly generous. I have seven rooms in total in my house and I empty it after each clean, it isn’t full to the top but it is pretty full so you can certainly do a full clean through the house without having to stop and empty the bin every five minutes.

The smaller 0.2 litre bin that is attached to the handheld section is ok, I find the limit is just doing the stairs with it before I need to empty it into the main bin, so if you’re planning on doing any areas that are heavily soiled, you may have to empty midway through the job which could get a little annoying after a while.

You can open and empty the small bin manually if you want, but to activate the self-emptying you just have to re-dock the wand onto the main body, so if you’re finished with cleaning, it makes more sense to just do it that way.

It has been revealed that this Shark does have a HEPA filter, and also the bin has an Anti-Allergen complete seal, so it catches and traps dust within the bin rather than pushing them back into the room. This makes it a great choice for anyone with allergies, but it’s also good to know that your hard work won’t be undone by emptying the bin.

In a recent development, one thing that’s worth noting is the weight. At a little over 17lbs, this isn’t a very lightweight vacuum when being used as an upright, so if you are going to move it between floors, then it’s worth just thinking about. However, the powered floorhead means that it’s light and easy to move across carpets; I certainly don’t feel like I’ve done a workout when I’ve finished vacuuming.

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer performed well on hard flooring. The built-in reveal lights do a good job of highlighting any dust and fur that can’t be seen by the naked eye. The head also glides around the flooring with ease and the auto-detect did a great job of recognising when the vacuum was going from hardwood to vinyl to tiles.

Vacuuming up the Rice Krispies and the seeds was ideal, it didn’t crush anything, just sucked it up in one go, making the job quick and easy. Nothing got pushed out to the sides either so it didn’t spread it across the floor.

This vacuum does incredibly well on carpeted floor. It's powerful suction gets deep in to the fibres and removes dust, debris, pet hair and anything else that may be hanging around. I was blown away how easily the vacuum picked up the test products. The Rice Krispies especially as they didn't get crushed to smashed in to the carpet, the moment the vacuum went over the top, it just sucked them up. It didn't have any problems picking up the chia seeds either which are small and could have easily been lost within the fibres but it vacuumed it all up leaving none behind. It was really interesting when it came to vacuuming up the hair as it also took in more debris that it found, and that was after the floor had already been vacuumed, so if there's anything on your carpet, this vacuum is going to suck it up.

Noise-wise, I don’t think this vacuum is over the top loud, I used the Decibel X app around 3 feet away from the vacuum and it recorded a reading of 71.1dB whilst it was cleaning.

If people are working or relaxing nearby, then it could be distracting, but it certainly isn’t the loudest vacuum that I’ve tested.

Sources indicate that despite being a three-in-one vacuum, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer doesn’t really need much space. It’s not the smallest vacuum, measuring 46.3 x 11.2 x 12.5 inches.

Industry observers note that but one advantage of it being a corded model is that it can be kept in its upright configuration and doesn’t need to be attached to the wall, placed on a charging dock, or be anywhere near a power outlet. I’ve stored mine under the stairs, and there’s plenty of room.

Shark has made some effort to think about how to store the accessories too. It ships with a bag so you can keep the additional tools together if you don’t want to risk them getting lost. But it also comes with some clips which create onboard accessory storage if you’d rather keep them with the unit. There are also dedicated hooks to keep the power cable tidy.

Maintenance is also pretty straightforward. The bin is bagless, so there’s no need to buy replacement bags. The bin also detaches from the main unit so you can take it outside directly to the bin to empty. You will want to clean the dust bin, as, speaking from my own experience, it does get very dusty. The bin lid opens from the bottom and the top so it’s easy to get a cloth in there and give it a good clean.

According to recent reports, the vacuum does have multiple filters, which are washable and require a little more maintenance. The filters are really easy to get out; they just pull out from their area, so there’s no real problem with removing them.

Industry observers note that as with most upright Shark vacuums, there is an anti-odor cartridge at the front of the floor head. This keeps things smelling fresh when the vacuum is running and needs to be replaced every six months. These cost $7.99/£7.99 direct from SharkNinja, but you can buy off-brand versions if you prefer.

Overall, this isn’t a machine that you’re going to have to spend a lot of time maintaining. But it is crucial to keep it clean and tidy so that you get the best performance out of it throughout its lifetime.

The Shark PowerDetect Transformer is an impressive upright cleaner, and you don’t have to compromise on the convenience of a stick or handheld.

Sources indicate that to say that this vacuum cleaner leaves nothing behind is an understatement. It performed consistently well across all three surfaces, collecting almost all of the test items that I laid down for it.

According to recent reports, it brings together an innovative design with a powerful performance that’s enough to convince me to ditch my cordless stick and go all in on this corded upright. I was really impressed by how well this vacuum got to work on carpets. It lifted embedded fur and dust that I had no idea was even there. I also found that being able to switch between different cleaning configurations made giving the house a full deep clean a lot easier.

There are a couple of drawbacks, of course: being corded means it’s not so easy to just grab it and vacuum up any small spills because you have to consciously get it out and plug it in. Also moving between floors is also a bit of a pain, again you have to carry it about.

However, when you consider that I managed to vacuum the whole house in under 20 minutes, that’s a pretty good indication that this vacuum does a great job quickly.

For anyone looking for the cleaning power of an upright with the flexibility of a stick and handheld vacuum, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer is a brilliant option.

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • In a recent development, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most crucial tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

In a recent development, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

It has been revealed that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

Recent findings suggest that first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

Recent findings suggest that the DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

It has been revealed that xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

Industry News: A Partial Evaluator for C

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 34 min read (6789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Labri

⏱️ ~34 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Partial evaluation is program transformation that automates a program specialization process.
  • Tempo is an off-line specializer; it is divided into two phases: analysis and specialization.
  • Recent findings suggest that following the analysis phase, the specialization phase generates a specialized program based on the annotated program and the values of the known inputs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What is Tempo? Partial evaluation is program transformation that automates a program specialization process. Tempo is a partial evaluator for C programs. It has been applied in various domains such as operating systems and networking, computer graphics, scientific computation, software engineering and domain specific languages. A first workshop on Tempo has been organized in March 1998. Tempo is now being distributed. Its documentation is available on line, as well as tutorial slides. An Overview of Tempo Tempo is a partial evaluator for C programs. It is being developed in the Compose project at IRISA / INRIA - LABRI (France). Tempo is an off-line specializer; it is divided into two phases: analysis and specialization. The input to the analysis phase consists of a program and a description of which inputs will be known during specialization and which will be unknown. Based on this knowledge, dependency analyses propagate information about known and unknown values throughout the code and produce an annotated program, indicating how each program construct should be transformed during specialization. Because C is an imperative language including pointers, the analysis phase performs alias and side-effect analyses in addition to binding-time analyses. The accuracy of these analyses is targeted towards keeping track of known values across procedures, data structures, and pointers. Following the analysis phase, the specialization phase generates a specialized program based on the annotated program and the values of the known inputs. Tempo can specialize programs at compile time (i.e., source-to-source tranformation) as well as run time (i.e., run-time binary code generation). For more details, please consider reading some of our papers, most of which are available at the following URL: papers. Program Analysis As a first step, the user provides a program and specifies what arguments (including global variables) are static. For example, the user provides the following code for a miniprintf function, and specifies in this way that the first argument is static whereas the second is dynamic: miniprintf(S,D). miniprintf(char fmt[], int val[]) {   int i = 0;   while( *fmt != '\0' ) {     if( *fmt != '%' )        putchar(*fmt);     else       switch(*++fmt) {         case 'd' : putint(val[i++]); break;                      case '%' : putchar('%');     break;         default  : prterror(*fmt);   break;       }     fmt++;   } } From this Tempo produces a program file with analysis annotations. These annotations can be visualized using colors that highlight the propagation of the known/unknown information throughout the program. /*  LEGEND:  STATIC  DYNAMIC  */ miniprintf(char fmt[], int val[]) {   int i = 0;   while( *fmt != '\0' ) {     if( *fmt != '%' )        putchar(*fmt);     else       switch(*++fmt) {         case 'd' : putint(val[i++]); break;                       case '%' : putchar('%');     break;         default  : prterror(*fmt);   break;       }     fmt++;   } } The blue color (bold face for black and white display) represent static constructions, i.e. values that can be computed at specialization time. The red color (standard font for black and white display) is for dynamic expressions, whose value cannot be precomputed knowing only the static arguments. Basically, everything in blue (bold) will disappear after specialization; only red (standard font) parts will remain. The visualization of the analysis is very important for the user to assess the amount of specialization in the code. Furthermore, the analysis speeds up the specialization process (as opposed to on-line partial evaluators). The analysis is inter-procedural and takes into account pointer aliases and side-effects. Compile-Time Specialization When the user is satisfied with the analysis (i.e., what the user expects to specialize indeed appears as static), actual specialization values must be provided. For example, giving "<%d,%d>" as the actual specialization value for the fmt argument of the miniprintf() function yields the following specialized code. miniprintf_1(int val[]) {   putchar( '<'    );   putint ( val[0] );   putchar( ','    );   putint ( val[1] );   putchar( '>'    ); } Many specializations can be made, sharing the same analysis. Only different specialization values have to be provided. Runtime Specialization Tempo can also perform runtime specialization, using optimized binary code templates. A dedicated runtime specializer is generated from the analysis of the program. In the case of the miniprintf function, Tempo generates a runtime specializer rts_miniprintf_1() which can be used as in the following example. /*  * Some dynamic execution context for variable 'format'  */ spec_printf = rts_miniprintf_1(format); ... (*spec_printf)(val1);   /* <=> miniprintf(format,val1) */ (*spec_printf)(val2);   /* <=> miniprintf(format,val2) */ The function rts_miniprintf_1() is a dedicated runtime specializer. It returns a pointer to the specialized function. Several specialized versions can also be generated and used at the same time. Applications of Tempo Tempo has been successfully applied in various domains, yielding substantial speedups. Operating system and networking: Sun RPC, Chorus IPC, BSD packet filter, Unix signals, active networks, Computer graphics (various filtering algorithms), Scientific computation (trajectory, FFT, math libraries), Software architectures and mechanisms: Domain specific languages GAL, BLUEPRINT-P), Selective broadcast (implicit invocation), Pattern matching, Interpreters, Software layers, Generic libraries. For an up-to-date list of non-confidential, published applications, please browse our ``papers'' web page: papers. Besides C, Tempo is right now being used as a back-end for specializing Java programs using Harissa, a JavaVM-to-C compiler. Fortran and C++ programs have also been specialized using translators to C. Projects Related to Tempo Cyclone Cyclone is a mobile code system being developed as part of the SwitchWare active-network project at the University of Pennsylvania. Cyclone uses two ideas to make mobile code safe as well as fast: run-time code generation and proof-carrying code. Cyclone relies on Tempo's analysis front-end (i.e. the binding-time analysis) and on TAL/T, an extension of the TAL typed assembly language. Workshop A workshop (actually closer to a ``winter school'') on Tempo has been organized at IRISA, March 16-18, 1998. The aim of this workshop was to present a three-day tutorial on Tempo and its applications to real size programs. We had 24 participants, coming from universities as well as industries. We believe it was a large success. The talks are now available on-line. Depending on request, if the distribution of Tempo is a success, we might organize another workshop later. It would less be like a ``winter school'' but rather like a real workshop with customers presenting applications and open discussions about possible improvements. It would be preceded by an optional one-day tutorial for people not knowing partial evaluation or Tempo. Distribution The Tempo specializer has been made publicly available under a licence in April 1998. At of March 99, it was being used by about thirty people around the world. The binary version of Tempo has just (July 2000) been made available without any restrictions, and we expect a full unrestricted source release under GPL to follow soon. Getting access to Tempo no longer requires signing a license agreement. Tempo is simply available via anonymous FTP, as described below. In any case, we would very much like to hear from you if you are an active Tempo user. If you are, please also let us know if and for what purpose you are using Tempo, by sending an email to tempo@labri.fr. We will by default add you to our tempo talk mailing list tempo-talk@labri.fr, where future Tempo releases will be unveiled, and Tempo users can discuss practical problems using Tempo. Tempo can be downloaded : Here is a Tempo release that have been made publicly available: i386 Linux Most recent Tempo binary distribution for i386 Linux (tested on RedHat 6.1). (Please remember to send an email to tempo@labri.fr to let us know who you are and why you are using Tempo. Remember to explicitly indicate if you are not interested in joining the tempo-talk@labri.fr mailing list.)   In case of any problem with getting or installing the distribution, get in touch with us: mailto:tempo@labri.fr References Here are general papers about Tempo and its architecture. More focused and up-to-date information regarding Tempo can be found in the main on-line papers tank. [CHN+96] A Uniform Approach for Compile-Time and Run-Time Specialization. Research Report 2775. INRIA, January 1996. C. Consel, L. Hornof, J. Noyé, F. Noel, and E.N. Volanschi. Revised version in Partial Evaluation, International Seminar, Dagstuhl Castle, LNCS 1110, Springer-Verlag, pages 54-72. [CHL+98] Tempo: Specializing Systems Applications and Beyond C. Consel, L. Hornof, J. Lawall, R. Marlet, G. Muller, J. Noyé, S. Thibault, N. Volanschi. To appear in ACM Computing Surveys, Symposium on Partial Evaluation, 1998. [CMVM97] Adaptabilité et évaluation partielle : Tempo, un spécialiseur pour le langage  C. C. Consel, G. Muller, N. Volanschi, R Marlet. Apr 1997. (In French.) Contact Information Developers and maintainers: tempo@labri.fr Tempo Specializer home page: tempo.

We believe it was a large success. The talks are now available on-line. Depending on request, if the distribution of Tempo is a success, we might organize another workshop later. It would less be like a ``winter school'' but rather like a real workshop with people presenting applications and open discussions about possible improvements. It would be preceded by an optional one-day tutorial for people not knowing partial evaluation or Tempo. Distribution The Tempo specializer has been made publicly available under a licence in April 1998. At of March 99, it was being used by about thirty people around the world. The binary version of Tempo has just (July 2000) been made available without any restrictions, and we expect a full unrestricted source release under GPL to follow soon. Getting access to Tempo no longer requires signing a license agreement. Tempo is simply available via anonymous FTP, as described below. LiberNovo’s Black Friday sale takes up to 42% off ergonomic chairs

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can spend plenty of time getting your Mac, display, and desk just right.
  • That’s the idea behind LiberNovo’s ergonomic chairs, which combine support that moves with you and a choice of sizes, including the Maxis range for bigger and taller consumers.
  • According to recent reports, adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can spend plenty of time getting your Mac, display, and desk just right. But what about the chair you use every day? Between typing, taking video calls, and leaning back to watch something, your position changes throughout the day. Your chair should be able to keep up.

That’s the idea behind LiberNovo’s ergonomic chairs, which combine support that moves with you and a choice of sizes, including the Maxis range for bigger and taller consumers. For Black Friday, LiberNovo is taking up to 42% off in the U.S., with chairs starting at $609 and offers running November 19–30.

According to recent reports, adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing. Keeping that support as you change position is another. LiberNovo’s Dynamic Support System links the neck support, backrest, armrests, and seat so they move together as you recline.

According to recent reports, the Bionic FlexFit Backrest adds eight flexible panels that contour independently. Rather than relying on a single rigid backrest, the design lets different sections follow your back as you shift or turn. Once you’ve adjusted the chair to fit, the system is designed to maintain contact through those movements with fewer manual readjustments.

According to recent reports, both the Omni and Maxis families offer five recline positions: 105, 115, 125, 135, and 160 degrees. That gives you options for desk work, a more relaxed position for watching a video, and a deeper recline for a break.

Recent findings suggest that A higher weight limit is only part of finding a chair that fits. Taller users also need enough seat depth, a headrest that reaches the right spot, and armrests with room to adjust.

According to recent reports, the LiberNovo Maxis range addresses those details with a 52 cm seat depth, a wider backrest with a flared base, and an extended-travel headrest with 140 mm of vertical adjustment and 120 mm of front-to-back adjustment. Its armrests sit lower and offer a wider, longer adjustment range to accommodate larger builds.

According to recent reports, liberNovo recommends Maxis for users approximately 5 feet 10 inches to 6 feet 7 inches tall, with a maximum supported weight of 399 pounds. Maxis is certified to BIFMA X5.11. The seat cushion uses firmer support at the rear and a softer front edge, while a six-spring Controlled Recline System is designed to build resistance progressively as you lean back.

In a recent development, for a shallower seat, the Omni family offers 45 cm and 48 cm configurations. Choosing between the two families starts with fit, then comes down to which features you want.

Industry observers note that there are three feature tiers in each family. Omni SE and Maxis Manual offer manually adjusted lumbar support, without a motor or battery. Both retain the flexible backrest, dynamic support, and five recline positions.

The Maxis Electric includes motorized lumbar adjustment and OmniStretch, a five-minute powered stretch sequence used in deep recline.

According to recent reports, omni Pro and Maxis Airflow add Active AirFlow seat ventilation. A fan draws air through the cushion to carry heat away, and an occupancy sensor pauses the fan when you stand up. These models also include a larger 3,000 mAh rechargeable battery.

LiberNovo’s warranty covers the frame and structural components for six years, and electronic components for two years.

Recent findings suggest that U.S. Black Friday prices run from November 19 through November 30. Here’s how the chair-only Basic Bundles compare:.

Bundles add another option. The Omni Pro Standard Bundle includes the chair and a footrest for $983. The Maxis Electric Premium Bundle includes the chair, a footrest, and an extra battery for $1,202, down from a listed MSRP of $2,086.

Industry observers note that liberNovo is also offering 30-day price protection on eligible purchases. U.S. gift tiers begin at $800 for a Mouse Pad, $1,000 for an Eco-Comfort three-piece gift set, and $1,200 for an Ergo-to-Go Travel Suite. Qualifying orders of $2,000, $3,000, or $4,000 receive an automatic additional saving of $60, $100, or $180, respectively, without a code.

U.S. shoppers can also choose Klarna Pay in 4 at 0% APR.

Ready to give your desk setup a more comfortable place to sit? Shop LiberNovo’s Black Friday sale to compare Omni and Maxis models, choose your fit, and explore the available bundles through November 30.

You Can Get One of These Pocket E-Readers for As Little As $55 Before Black Friday

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (736 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a fresh e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a massive discount are low.
  • If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price.
  • Sources indicate that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a fresh e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a massive discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Sources indicate that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

In a recent development, the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

Recent findings suggest that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also key to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

According to recent reports, no. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Artist and filmmaker Allison Janae Hamilton has set her next project, a narrative short titled Holler, starring Edwina Findley and musician Valerie June. The film will be produced under Hamilton’s newly minted production company, Swampwife Pictures.

Recent findings suggest that set against the rural landscape of West Tennessee, the film follows a hard-living Memphis nightclub owner who returns to her family’s land when signs of a once-in-a-generation ecological event begin to emerge. Called home to perform a ritual demanded by her lineage, she must confront both the ancestral responsibilities she has inherited and the person she left behind without saying goodbye. Related Stories News Allison Janae Hamilton Discusses Her Latest Film Project 'Venus Of Ossabaw' & How She Plans To Reach Audiences In The "Popular Arena" With Her Debut Feature 'Floridaland' News Rotterdam Hires Pepijn Kuyper As Managing Director.

Hamilton wrote and directed the contemporary Western, which stars Findley and June alongside Sheria Irving and Aysia Moorer, with Jaselle Martino (Abdo and Saneya) of Chaconia Pictures producing in collaboration with Hamilton’s Swampwife Pictures. Antonino D’Ambrosio of La Lutta Productions (Roberta) is an Exec Producer. Watch on Deadline.

Hamilton is a 2026 Guggenheim Fellow. Her previous short film, Venus of Ossabaw, debuted in March 2026 at Telfair Museums in Savannah, Georgia. She is currently adapting the short into a feature. Hamilton is also in development on Floridaland, another feature script she has penned. The project was selected as part of the Sundance Institute’s 2026 Screenwriters Intensive.

“The elements that these films have in common form the cornerstone of what I want to do with Swampwife, which is to tell stories rooted in the land, driven by character, and that expand our ideas of genre,” Hamilton told Deadline.

“I want Swampwife to be known for stories that feel like stepping into another world, one of richly layered visuals and emotionally resonant characters. Swampwife gives all my storytelling interests a single home.”.

The Holler creative team also includes cinematographer Nikita Carpenter, who previously collaborated with Hamilton on Venus of Ossabaw; production designer Freyja Bardell, whose recent credits include the feature film Is God Is (2026) and Kendrick Lamar’s Not Like Us music video; and casting director Damian Bao, known for his work on The Man I Love, Forge, Love Me, Look Into My Eyes, Port Authority, Goldie, and American Honey.

Holler will debut in Spring 2027 as part of Hamilton’s forthcoming solo exhibition, A Slow Drag for the Conjure Women, at the Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia (ICA).

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to customers on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

Sources indicate that whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the patch becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the firm revealed four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save major on a few worthy Kindle alternatives.
  • In a recent development, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save major on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

In a recent development, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the tech giant introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

Sources indicate that if you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

According to recent reports, if you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is at the moment $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The upcoming Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Sources indicate that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's right now pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (at the moment $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Sources indicate that no. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

If You Loved 'Phony,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
