💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us.
  • Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).
  • A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us. When someone close to us suddenly, imperceptibly shifts, it can be unsettling, especially because you can’t be sure what’s changed or why. Those are the waters where Hulu’s Phony swims, delivering a perfectly pitched dramedy about a teenager (Sam Nivola) who emerges from a brief coma convinced that his mother (a pitch-perfect Connie Britton) has been replaced with a double. If you loved the series (and similar shows) and you’re looking for more intriguing stories about doubles and impostors close to home, you should definitely watch Goodnight Mommy.

Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).

A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before. The boys also find clues that bolster their fears, including a photograph showing their mother posing with a woman dressed identically to her.

The boys’ attempts to force her to confess rapidly descend into a kind of madness, ultimately leading them to tie her to the bed in an effort to force her to admit she’s not their real mother. It all leads to a reveal as affecting as Phony’s ultimate explanation (albeit a lot more grim and violent). The film goes way harder than the series, but if you were totally into the premise, this is the more horrifying version you’ll want to see. The original film is German; there was a 2022 remake starring Naomi Watts, and while it's pretty good, the original is the right choice. Stream Goodnight Mommy on Kanopy or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that looking for more impostor stories that dig into the psychological and emotional impact of suspecting someone has been replaced? Here are a few more movies that dig into the concept.

The Hole in the Ground offers an inversion: A mother who becomes convinced that her son has been replaced by an impostor. Firmly in the supernatural horror genre, the story still plays the same game with the viewer: Is Sarah (Seána Kerslake) crazy, or has her son, Chris (James Quinn Markey), been replaced by a creature living in the woods near their home? It’s got the same disturbing energy as Sarah struggles with how much her son’s changed behavior is her own psychological projection and how much is clear evidence that he’s no longer the same person—or, possibly, even the same species. Stream The Hole in the Ground on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, taking a slightly more literary approach (it’s based on a novella by Fyodor Dostoyevsky), The Double explores what happens if you find yourself replaced by a doppelgänger. Simon (Jesse Eisenberg) is a nonentity—ignored at work, lonely, and silently longing for the girl living across the street, Hannah (Mia Wasikowska). One day, a latest employee named James appears at Simon’s job—and James looks exactly like Simon. But James is assertive, confident, and charming, sending Simon into a spiral. As the two versions slide into a battle for dominance, Simon finds himself turning to increasingly deranged moves to rid himself of the new and improved version of himself. If you loved the psychological implications that Phony explores, check out The Double. Stream The Double on Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that on one level, Denis Villeneuve’s 2013 film is about a college professor named Adam (Jake Gyllenhaal) who discovers an actor named Anthony who looks exactly like him (also played by Gyllenhaal). When he tracks his double down, their lives merge in messy ways, ending in tragedy and one of the most striking (and confusing) final shots in cinema history. On another level, Enemy is a deft trick, exploring someone’s subconscious using dream logic and misdirection. If the best part about Phony was the disorienting sense that a secret just under the surface will explain everything, Enemy is the perfect choice. Stream Enemy on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for a deeper, crazier, and more terrifying story about doubles, Andrzej Żuławski’s 1981 film is a terrific choice. Inspired in part by his own feelings in the wake of a painful divorce, the story follows Mark (Sam Neil), a spy who returns to West Berlin at the height of the Cold War only to find out his wife, Anna (Isabelle Adjani), has been having an affair and wants a divorce. But Anna’s behavior becomes increasingly strange, and then Mark meets their son’s teacher, Helen, who looks just like Anna. And that’s before Anna kind of ... grows a replacement Mark from a tentacled creature kept in her bathroom (and that’s just the beginning of how weird this movie gets), resulting in two doubles. How much of the film is meant literally and how much simply represents the trauma of romantic betrayal and divorce is up to you, but Possession will definitely leave a mark. Stream Possession on Shudder, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that obsession looks at the Doppelgänger Effect from a different perspective. Cliff Robertson plays Michael Courtland, a wealthy businessman whose wife (Geneviève Bujold) and young daughter, Amy (Wanda Blackman), are kidnapped in 1959. When he follows police advice against delivering the ransom, both appear to be killed in an explosion. Courtland spends the next 16 years hating himself, until he encounters a young woman, Sandra (also Bujold), who looks almost exactly like his late wife. He works to make Sandra look as much like his wife as possible, and eventually proposes—but then Sandra is kidnapped in precisely the same way as his wife and daughter sixteen years before. This all leads to a head-spinning series of reveals and a twist that echoes the Hitchcock classic Vertigo. Rent Obsession on Prime Video.

ITV has said its duty of care to I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! contestants is of the “utmost importance” amid concern over an incident between campmates AJ Odudu and Mariella Frostrup.

On Sunday evening, ITV broadcast footage of tensions between Big Brother host Odudu and broadcaster Frostrup over camp cooking duties (see below).

During one exchange, Frostrup accused Odudu of being “aggressive” and creating a “drama out of a crisis.” Odudu implored Frostrup not to “use those words towards me,” adding: “‘Dramatic’ and ‘aggressive’ are very harsh words.” Related Stories News Gordon Ramsay Teams With 'The Traitors' Host Claudia Winkleman To Reboot 'Hell's Kitchen' On ITV News 'Bridgerton' Star Adjoa Andoh Co-Creating & Starring In ITV Detective Drama 'Protect And Serve'.

Sources indicate that the duo attempted to hash it out in a later conversation, during which Frostrup apologized. “Please don’t call me aggressive,” Odudu asked. “Only if you’re not being aggressive,” Frostrup replied. “So you stand by that?” Odudu added. “We’ll agree to disagree on that one.” Watch on Deadline.

Frostrup mentioned: “I just said — if you stop [talking] for a second — I just said: If it upset you, I apologize. So can you bank that, so you know that I said that.” Frostrup later told viewers that she hoped the matter was resolved.

Sources indicate that odudu’s experience prompted an outcry on social media. On Instagram, Strictly Come Dancing judge Motsi Mabuse wrote: “I wish there were better ways to protect ourselves from microaggressions and the cumulative emotional toll they take.

Industry observers note that “It’s a weight that many will never fully understand, and sadly, some won’t even try. The exhaustion comes not only from experiencing it, but also from constantly having to explain why it hurts.”.

It has been revealed that comedian Judi Love mentioned: “This is so loaded. And yet @ajodudu is the person who first apologised. Very uncomfortable to watch.” Alesha Dixon, a judge on Britain’s Got Talent, added: “@ajodudu for the win … Mariella in the bin!”.

Recent findings suggest that presenter Clara Amfo stated: “Calling a Black woman ‘aggressive’ when she is being anything but is a classic microaggression. Mariella’s tears, doubling down and then doing ’sorry if,’ woefully predictable. This is deeply uncomfortable.”.

In a statement, an ITV spokesperson noted: “The production monitors everyone in camp 24/7 and if at any time we feel someone has overstepped the line by using inappropriate language or displaying unacceptable behaviour, we would take steps to intervene and speak to everyone involved.

Sources indicate that “The duty of care for our contestants is of the utmost importance to us. We take the welfare of the celebrities very seriously and have measures in place to ensure they are supported at every stage of the process: before, during and after filming.”.

Sources indicate that apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and people who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Sources indicate that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

It has been revealed that the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Sources indicate that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

#142656. Elegoo's Centauri 2 Combo delivers multi-color 3D printing on a budget — but you might miss the enclosure

Elegoo's Centauri 2 Combo delivers multi-color 3D printing on a budget — but you might miss the enclosure

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, elegoo's Centauri 2 Combo delivers very solid print quality and four-color printing for under $380.
  • In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you.
  • Recent findings suggest that 3D printing has been edging closer and closer to the mainstream for years now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, elegoo's Centauri 2 Combo delivers very solid print quality and four-color printing for under $380. Inevitably given that low price, certain corners are cut. None of these are deal-breakers, but there are better printers on the market — including quite a few from Elegoo — for only a little bit more cash. Still, if you're on a tight budget or are a beginner who is interested in multi-color printing, this is a decent choice.

Multi-color printing generates a lot of waste.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Recent findings suggest that 3D printing has been edging closer and closer to the mainstream for years now. It's cheaper than ever to buy a really good, feature-packed machine, while the various manufacturers are constantly working to try and make their products easier to use and more accessible.

Recent findings suggest that despite that, it can still feel like a comparative niche to newcomers, and getting to grips with your first 3D printer can be... intimidating. Enter Elegoo's Centauri line, which has been around since 2024. These are designed to bring 3D printing to the masses, with easy to use machines at affordable prices.

Industry observers note that the Centauri Carbon 2 Combo launched at the start of the year and was a very impressive model for its $449 RRP, but the manufacturer has recently upped the ante with an even-more-budget offering that does most of what its predecessor can do for under $380 — and you can already find it cheaper than that in some of the sales. But does that low price point come with any downsides?

Find out in my full Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo review.

According to recent reports, it really is quite impressive what this printer can do. It delivers easy setup, good build quality, and multi-color 3D printing at such a low price point.

Recent findings suggest that the most obvious selling point of the Centauri 2 Combo is its four-color printing. You simply attach the spool holders to the top of the machine, pop on your filament and then feed them into each extruder.

If you're using official Elegoo spools with RFID tags, then the CANVAS unit (Elegoo’s filament switching system) on the top of the machine will automatically identify which color is which. You then simply feed the filament into the numbered inlets on the machine. The results are good, with well-defined color changes. My first print was a classic Benchy, which printed quickly and cleanly in 45 minutes.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Next up, I printed two Daleks from Doctor Who, based on a nice fan-made model that I found on Cults3D by user wayne_peters.

The red one was printed using the factory standard printer settings. For the yellow I tweaked several settings for surface ironing and adaptive layers in the hope of getting a smoother print. That significantly upped the print time, but didn't deliver massively different results. If you’re noticing some rough edges, those were me being a bit slapdash post print, not an issue with the printer.

According to recent reports, one thing to note is that printing models with multiple colors will significantly increase the amount of waste filament produced, because of the way the printer has to switch between colors. That's not a criticism of the Centauri 2 Combo, it's just the nature of the technology. If you are concerned about filament wastage then printing models with multi-colored parts may not be for you.

The Centauri 2 Combo arrived securely packaged and was very easy to assemble. I'd say it was a seamless experience, except for one small but really quite frustrating aspect that added a good 15 minutes of swearing onto the build.

In a recent development, that was attaching the filament hub. You have to fix it into place with two tiny screws, one of which feels almost impossible to get into position because of the way the cable drag chain is positioned. I really struggled with this, almost losing the screw several times, before finally somehow managing to get it into place.

Industry observers note that thankfully after that, everything ran perfectly smoothly. When you first switch the machine on it runs through a self-check and calibration, as well as levelling the bed automatically. That really takes the stress out of the setup and is another reason why this is a good machine for beginners.

After setup, you need to install two pieces of software: ElegooSlicer on your computer and Elegoo Matrix on a smartphone.

Recent findings suggest that elegooSlicer is the software used to work on your 3D models (which can be downloaded from sites like Printables, Makerworld, and Elegoo's own Nexprint) before exporting them ready to be printed. It's based on the open-source OrcaSlicer and is intuitive enough for newcomers to get to grips with swiftly.

Industry observers note that elegoo Matrix enables you to monitor and control your printer remotely and is pretty fool proof. Again, you get the sense of a system that has been designed with novices in mind.

I can't stress how straightforward this printer is, as it does most of the hard work for you automatically. If this is your first 3D printer then it won't take you very long to get used to it, and if you've used one of Elegoo's other printers before, particularly any of the Centauri models, then you'll have no worries.

I printed the Halloween skeleton candlestick below, found on Nexprint, in a little over seven hours — pretty good for such an intricate design!

According to recent reports, A curvy vase, also from Nexprint, was equally straightforward and printed in just over three hours, with no need for the supports that you would typically need to include with complex prints. I've since used the machine to print out some gaming terrain as well as for practical applications like paint storage for my Warhammer paints and storage boxes.

According to recent reports, over several weeks of use and around 30 prints I had only one fail. I cancelled the print, tried again and the second time it worked with no problems.

Despite the low price point, the Centauri 2 Combo doesn't feel cheap. There are some cut corners — we'll come to those in a moment — but it's a reassuringly solid piece of kit, robustly built from a die-cast aluminum frame and steel body. Once again, it recalls Elegoo's bestselling Centauri 2 Combo Carbon in its design, which feels similarly solid.

The build-plate is double-sided (textured on side A and smooth on side B) and made from magnetic spring steel that's easy to keep clean. The toolhead comes with a standard 0.4mm hardened steel nozzle, which can be swapped out for different sizes, which are sold separately. You will also need to buy a nozzle wrench to do that.

It feels almost churlish to complain about the Centauri 2 Combo as it's really very good at what it sets out to do — and there's no arguing with that aggressive price point. Even so, there are a few reasons why you might want to consider shelling out for a slightly more expensive machine.

Probably the biggest talking point with the Centauri 2 Combo is the price — but it comes at the cost of several features that you'd usually find on a 3D printer.

According to recent reports, the most obvious of these omissions is the lack of an enclosure. The panels, glass door and hood are all absent, meaning that the print bed is exposed for all to see. In this way it echoes the design of several competitors, including Anycubic's Kobra X and Creality's 3D SparkX i7 Combo. That mentioned, I much prefer the neat and tidy design of the Centauri 2 Combo.

According to recent reports, there's something quite cool about being able to watch your latest print materialise right there in front of you without it being hidden away behind glass, but enclosures are useful for maintaining temperatures and containing the fumes from a print. If you're sticking to printing with standard PLA it's no biggie (though please still ventilate your space), but if you're using other types of filament you may feel more comfortable investing in a printer that comes with an enclosure.

The other downside is that you'll also have to make sure you either cover the printer after use, or dust it regularly.

Other features that are absent from this model include a camera (fun and useful for monitoring your prints while away from home, and something that is notably included on the Creality 3D SparkX i7 Combo) and internal lights.

In a recent development, neither of these things are deal-breakers and I think newcomers, in particular, will find a lot to love in the Centauri 2 Combo. But if you're serious about 3D printing then you may find yourself rapidly considering upgrading to a more capable machine. The Centauri 2 Combo is entering an increasingly crowded 3D printer market — with much of the competition coming from Elegoo itself.

The obvious competitor here is the almost identically titled Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo. For a mere $70 more right now you can pick that machine up and enjoy a printer with an enclosure, wider filament compatibility, camera and a HEPA + Activated Carbon filter.

Single-color printing with PLA tends to be fairly efficient, when it comes to waste. That changes significantly when you move to multi-color printing, however, because of the way the printer has to switch between colors. That's not a criticism of the Centauri 2 Combo, it's just the nature of the technology.

Recent findings suggest that basically, when the printer needs to change colors, it retracts the filament being currently used, nips the end off it and ejects the waste, before loading in the fresh color. If you're printing something with a lot of differently-colored parts (even if you're just using 2 or 3 colors) then it is going to do this a lot. Your waste basked will fill up swiftly and if you are concerned about filament wastage (which is difficult to recycle) then printing models with multi-colored parts may not be for you. The picture above is mostly the waste from my two model Daleks!

It has been revealed that one way to get around this, if you're printing model kits or things that can be glued together, is by printing each color separately. That will save you both print time and filament wastage, but will not be possible with everything you might want to print.

The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo is defined by its price point. It's pretty remarkable that you can get a good four-color 3D printer for under over $400 (and sometimes a lot under that price, with Elegoo's occasional discounts). That figure may prove very tempting for those looking to get into printing for the first time.

Recent findings suggest that the price, however, is also behind some of the machine's rougher edges. The lack of an enclosure may not seem like much, but it means that the Centauri 2 Combo really needs to be positioned in a well-ventilated room if you don't want to be inhaling fumes all the time. I can't quibble too much at the lack of a camera or internal lights — at this price, those are nice to have features, rather than essentials.

It has been revealed that if you're serious about 3D printing then there are more fully-featured machines out there that may catch your eye. But if you’re newly introduced to all this and want a printer that can handle everyday use, as well as more complex prints, it really is hard to find much to grumble about here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Sixty-years in the making, post-production is nearing completion on feature thriller The Wrong People, an adaptation of the 1967 novel of the same name by Robin Maugham, a dark thriller exposing trafficking in North Africa in the sixties.

In a recent development, first announced as a feature film in 1972, the project was shot in-and-around London and Essaouira, Morocco, in early 2026, with cast including Luke Newberry (Anna Karenina), Caroline Goodall (Schindler’s List), Alec Newman (The Weight), Calum Ross (Wednesday), Branka Katic (The King’s Man) and Joe Anderson (Across the Universe). Related Stories News ITV Issues Statement Amid Outcry Over AJ Odudu Experiencing "Microaggressions" On 'I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here!' News Allison Janae Hamilton Launches Production Outfit Swampwife Pictures & Sets 'Holler' Starring Valerie June As First Project.

According to recent reports, steven Fierberg, the veteran cinematographer of movies including Secretary and Love & Other Drugs and hit series including The Affair and Emily In Paris, has directed the film from a script written by David Griffin. Pic is being produced by Stephen Israel (Swimming with Sharks) via his production firm School Pictures, alongside Ioanna Karavela (Bad Day at the Office). Executive producers are Brett Husbands and Tom Abell of LGBTQ specialist Peccadillo, which is handling UK & Irish distribution rights. Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, the Wrong People “follows Arnold Turner (Newberry), a gay boarding-school teacher in England who travels to Tangier in search of respite from repression in the UK, where homosexuality remains illegal. There he befriends expat Lavinia Morris (Goodall) and falls in with the wealthy Clarence Baird (Newman), only to find himself blackmailed in the city’s darker corners into trafficking one of his students, Dan (Ross), to Morocco, a plan that has devastating consequences.”.

Maugham’s first explicitly gay-themed novel garnered controversy at the time of its publication given that homosexuality was still illegal in Britain for most of the 1960s.

Originally published under a pseudonym after Somerset Maugham advised his nephew Robin Maugham “they will kill you”, the well-received novel was championed by Oscar nominee Sal Mineo (Rebel Without a Cause), who spent many years trying to get the project financed before his untimely death in 1976. More recently, we wrote about the project six years ago as having a script by veteran UK screenwriter David McGillivray. The producers of this version of the movie acquired the rights from McGillivray.

War veteran and politician Maugham (the nephew of popular British playwright and novelist Somerset Maugham) is probably best known in film and literary circles for his novella The Servant which was the basis for the 1963 Jospeh Losey film of the same name with Dirk Bogarde, James Fox and Sarah Miles. He died in 1981.

“The team has worked for many years to make this project a reality,” noted Israel who added, “we are excited to have finally achieved what Sal had hoped for. We dedicate this film to him.”.

Sources indicate that “Steven and I have long wanted to work together,” he noted. “I’m grateful we get to work on such an important addition to the canon of queer cinema.”.

“I feel incredibly fortunate to have Alec Newman, Luke Newberry, Caroline Goodall and the wonderfully gifted Calum Ross joining us,” said Fierberg. “It’s truly a dream cast. The story examines the depravity of human nature which some will exploit, and the corrosive effects of criminalizing sexual orientation.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

In a recent development, not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

It has been revealed that when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be said for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Sources indicate that because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before fresh models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

It has been revealed that price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

According to recent reports, in the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The concern isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

The key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a newly introduced tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

Recent findings suggest that to avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

Sources indicate that if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

According to recent reports, yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In a recent development, yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

In a recent development, black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Industry observers note that 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

It has been revealed that as my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final upgrade.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-latest design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 customers, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

In a recent development, for Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week aims based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo consumers, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Recent findings suggest that reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Recent findings suggest that finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The revision also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the patch expands Siri AI with many newly introduced capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these newly introduced capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so people can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Recent findings suggest that today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to upcoming languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

It has been revealed that you can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a newly introduced vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music people, iOS 27.3 adds a newly introduced “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the patch introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a newly introduced “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These two files are the whole claim. Statements.lean defines four propositions. Main.lean proves them, and Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis, by citing theorems from the other 175,185 modules. Point at a symbol to see how to say it and what type it has.

In a recent development, in words: every zero of the Riemann zeta function, other than the trivial zeros −2, −4, −6, … , has real part ½. For every Dirichlet character χ, every zero of L(s, χ) with real part strictly between 0 and 1 has real part ½.

Each rectangle is one module. Modules are grouped by directory, and a larger rectangle means more of the chosen size measure.

Scroll over the map to zoom, drag to move, click a module to read its code.

It has been revealed that terms come from Alpöge's announcement and from standard number theory. A module is counted if the term's identifier appears in its text, not counting import lines.

Where each step appears to live in the Lean code, according to a blueprint of the proof by GitHub user jae-63. ● found clearly   ◐ names and position fit   ○ weak evidence. The number is how many modules match. Point at a step to see it on the map; click to keep it highlighted.

Each module's field is predicted by a classifier from the Mathlib and project identifiers it uses. The prediction agrees with a language model's reading of the module about half the time (details under Sources and method). Point at a row to see where that field sits on the map.

Sources indicate that the line under each field lists objects and theorems named in the labels that a language model gave to each of 746 directories after reading a digest of its identifiers. Treat them as a guide, not a census.

A comment on Hacker News reported 204 modules "not referenced anywhere", without a list or a method. In the import graph no module is unreferenced: every module except Main.lean is imported by at least one other module. The comment may be counting something that imports do not show, such as declarations that nothing uses.

Scroll the graph sideways to see all of it.

Colour the map by numeric literals per 100 lines or by share of characters that are the digits 0–9.

Point at a bar to see what the tactic does and which modules use it.

In a recent development, what each of these public pages reported when read on 23 November 2026. None of the checks were run in building this page.

The Lean statements cover the Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions. They do not cover Dedekind zeta functions or automorphic L-functions.

It has been revealed that ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Frontline Features will debut the Oscar-contending documentary One in a Million for free on its YouTube channel ahead of the film’s PBS broadcast, in an unprecedented move.

Raney Aronson-Rath, Frontline editor-in-chief and executive producer, commented, “We’ve been publishing all our full documentaries on YouTube for nearly a decade, building a highly engaged, consistent, and growing audience hungry for the stories we tell. One in a Million marks an exciting first for FRONTLINE: releasing a feature documentary on YouTube ahead of its broadcast premiere. It feels like exactly the right film to break new ground, bringing Itab and Jack’s extraordinary documentary directly to our digital audience after the incredible response it has received from festival and theatrical audiences.” Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, one in a Million premiered at Sundance, where it won the Audience Award for World Cinema Documentary and the directing award in that category, recognizing Azzam and MacInnes. It has been honored at Sheffield DocFest in the UK, the Montclair Film Festival in Latest Jersey, and the Dallas International Film Festival; both DOC NYC and the IDA Documentary Awards have named One in a Million to their shortlists of the year’s best documentaries.

The film, shot over a 10-year period, follows protagonist Israa from childhood to adulthood “on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again,” notes a synopsis. “We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self.”.

According to recent reports, frontline, American television’s longest running investigative documentary series, is produced at GBH in Boston and is broadcast nationwide on PBS. Its 2023 film 20 Days in Mariupol, directed by Mstyslav Chernov, won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature. The series has won 113 Emmys and 35 Peabody Awards.

Frontline’s Aronson-Rath will be a guest on Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast on Tuesday, December 1, discussing the success of the series and the worldwide acclaim for One in a Million.

  • Macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the manufacturer’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….

Macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

Recent findings suggest that it’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.).

I’m a substantial fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy owners at least would like a little more transparency and control.

Sources indicate that airPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant patch in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, owners had to wait until it “just worked.”.

Sources indicate that apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an upgrade, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

In a recent development, make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

In a recent development, another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

According to recent reports, I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that presently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

  • It has been revealed that the film, which is China’s submission for the Best International Feature category of the Oscars, also scooped Best Actor for Shen Tang’s performance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Chinese drama Once Upon A Time In The Middle East, directed by Wen Muye, walked away with the top award, the Snow Leopard for Best Film, at this year’s Asian World Film Festival (AWFF) in Culver City, Los Angeles.

It has been revealed that the film, which is China’s submission for the Best International Feature category of the Oscars, also scooped Best Actor for Shen Tang’s performance. Set in a fictional Middle East city, it tells the story of a Chinese chef whose restaurant becomes a refuge when war breaks out.

Previous winners of the Best Film Snow Leopard have included Lebanon’s A Sad And Beautiful World in 2025 and Malaysia’s Abang Adik the previous year. Related Stories News Asian World Film Festival Reveals Asian Vision & Focus On Sections News Asian World Film Festival Unveils Competition Line-up; Kyrgyzstan's 'Kassandra' Set As Opening Film.

Best Actress in the Snow Leopard competition went to Nazifa Tushi for her role in Bangladesh drama Roid, directed by Mejbaur Rahman Sumon, which also won acclaim when it premiered at this year’s Rotterdam film festival. Watch on Deadline.

Iraqi action thriller No Paradise If You Are Killed By A Woman, directed by Halkawt Mustafa, took home the Snow Leopard Special Jury Prize.

Israeli writer-director Moshe Rosenthal was presented with the Snow Leopard Jury Discretionary Award for Best Screenplay for Tell Me Everything. The family drama, which premiered at Sundance film festival, revolves around a 12-year-old boy who discovers his father is having a relationship with another man.

U.S. audiences honored Poh Si Teng’s documentary American Doctor, a co-production between the U.S., Palestine, Malaysia and Qatar, about three American physicians who worked out of a Gaza hospital before and after the 2025 ceasefire. Dr. Rizk Abu Shaaira, a Palestinian surgeon featured in the film, was reportedly killed in a Gaza hospital strike last week.

In the festival’s Asia Vision section, the top award was presented to fact-based Kyrgyz drama Kurak, co-directed by Erke Dzhumakmatova and Emil Atageldijev.

It has been revealed that lebanese filmmaker Samah El Kadi’s coming-of-age story Baadarane won the Best Short Film Award, which came with a $3,000 WDA Entertainment studio credit. Two additional shorts – Nava, directed by Dena Rassam, and Touch, from Mohammad Davoodi Kia – both Iranian films, received special mentions.

According to recent reports, armenian-U.S. producer Arthur M. Sarkissian headed the feature film jury, while French-Chinese producer Celine Zen served as short film jury president.

Among the stars and executives who walked the red carpet were breakout actress Mason Reeves (Josephine); Kyrgyz director Artykpai Suyundukov; veteran actor John Savage (The Deer Hunter); actress Irene Tsu (Down & Out in Beverly Hills); writer-director Moshe Rosenthal; actress, stunt performer and filmmaker Diana Lee Inosanto (The Mandalorian); actor and stunt performer Simon Rhee (Mission: Impossible III); actor Mark Irvingsen (Finding Normal); and producer Andre Morgan (Walker, Texas Ranger).

The gala celebration was emceed by Mico Saad, TV host, actor and filmmaker, and Maria Shantanova, actress and model.

It has been revealed that AWFF’s closing night gala capped a week of around 60 screenings from more than 33 Asian nations and autonomous regions, along with filmmaker Q&As. The line-up included 27 official submissions for the Best International Feature Film category of the Oscars.

Recent findings suggest that this year, AWFF also presented its first-ever official Focus On Kazakhstan program, featuring the world premiere of The Nomad’s Legacy, an action thriller written and directed by Marina Kunarova, and the U.S. premiere of Elzat Eskendir’s Abel, which is Kazakhstan’s official Oscars submission.

In a recent development, shannon Lee, chairperson of the Bruce Lee Foundation, presented the Bruce Lee Award to Diana Lee Inosanto. Mason Reeves was presented with the Rising Star Award. Other honorees included Kyrgyz director Artykpai Suyundukov, who received the Lifetime Achievement Award, and Chinese-U.S. actress Irene Tsu who received an award for Outstanding Cinematic Achievement.

According to recent reports, “We founded AWFF because we wanted audiences to share in the excitement we felt about films from across Asia and the Asian diaspora,” stated AWFF executive director Georges N. Chamchoum.

“Watching this year’s lineup, we felt that excitement all over again. Asian artists continue to fuel the stories, the energy and imagination of world cinema, and it was a joy to close the week by honoring the very best of their work.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I’ve used Apple’s Calendar app for years, and there’s an elegant simplicity to it. But one key area the app has long lagged behind competitors is event creation.

According to recent reports, when you need to create a new event, the Calendar app historically has required manually filling in various fields for the title, date, time, invitees, etc. By contrast, the excellent third-party app Fantastical lets you type in natural language and it automatically fills in relevant parameters based on what you type.

In iOS 27, Apple finally introduces its own natural language input for Calendar events. You can type out your event details and certain recognized parameters will be used to automatically fill in the detail fields.

While the feature still isn’t on par with what Fantastical offers, since it doesn’t support as many data points as the third-party alternative, it’s very much a step in the right direction.

Sources indicate that apple has always pitched Siri as being like a personal assistant. As such, calendar-related tasks should have been Siri’s strong suit. But until iOS 27, you couldn’t actually manage your calendar very well using Siri.

Industry observers note that with Siri AI, that’s changed in a substantial way. Now, you can do things like:.

One of my favorite personal examples is from this summer when the NFL schedule was released. I asked Siri to find the Dallas Cowboys schedule and add every game to my calendar, and it pulled this off with ease.

Siri is so much better than before at assisting with your calendar, and iOS 27.3 will bring even more capabilities soon.
